task.title: Intra-rule slice and pointer aliasing of Transforms across Content and PCRE matchers
task.body:
### Description

    When parsing rules with sticky buffer transformations (e.g., `to_lowercase`, `dotprefix`, `url_decode`), `parser.go` assigns the active `[]*Transform` slice directly to each `Content` and `PCRE` matcher without cloning the slice or its elements:

    ```go
    con := &Content{
        DataPosition: st.dataPosition,
        Pattern:      c,
        Negate:       negate,
        Options:      options,
        Transforms:   st.activeTransforms,
    }
    ```
    *(and similarly for `PCRE` matchers: `p.Transforms = st.activeTransforms`)*

    Because all matchers under the same sticky buffer share the same underlying `[]*Transform` backing array and `*Transform` pointers, two aliasing issues can occur:

    1. **Post-parse AST mutation affects sibling matchers**:
       If a rule has multiple `content` or `pcre` matchers sharing a sticky buffer (e.g. `http.uri; to_lowercase; content:"foo"; content:"bar";`), both `Content` structs point to the exact same `[]*Transform` backing array and `*Transform` structs. Modifying `r.Contents()[0].Transforms[0]` or appending to `r.Contents()[0].Transforms` (when spare slice
  capacity exists) unintentionally mutates `r.Contents()[1].Transforms`.

    2. **Backing array overwrites when transforms are interleaved with matchers**:
       Once `st.activeTransforms` has spare capacity (e.g., `len == 2, cap == 4` after appending two transforms), if a subsequent transform is encountered before another matcher on the same buffer, `append(st.activeTransforms, ...)` mutates the shared backing array in place. Any caller that appends a single element to an earlier matcher's `Transforms` slice
  will collide with the shared backing array.

    ### Example Reproduction

    ```go
    r, err := ParseRule(`alert http any any -> any any (msg:"test"; http.uri; to_lowercase; content:"a"; content:"b"; sid:1; rev:1;)`)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Mutating the transform on the first content match unintentionally mutates the second content match.
    r.Contents()[0].Transforms[0].Name = "to_uppercase"

    // Fail: r.Contents()[1].Transforms[0].Name is now also "to_uppercase"
    ```

    ### Proposed Fix

    Create a deep copy (or fresh slice with cloned `Transform` structs) when attaching `activeTransforms` to a `Content` or `PCRE` matcher, e.g.:

    ```go
    func cloneTransforms(src []*Transform) []*Transform {
        if len(src) == 0 {
            return nil
        }
        dst := make([]*Transform, len(src))
        for i, t := range src {
            cp := *t
            dst[i] = &cp
        }
        return dst
    }
    ```

spec: Intra-rule slice and pointer aliasing of Transforms across Content and PCRE matchers
